primary_citation: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code §17500 (Stats. 1941, Ch. 807; amended through Prop 64 (2004))
short_title: False Advertising Law (FAL) — Untrue or Misleading Statements to the Public
one_line_rule: Any person making a statement about goods or services to the public that is untrue or misleading, and which they know or should know is untrue or misleading, violates California law; injured consumers may seek injunction and restitution.

case_law.key_rule: Three-part commercial speech test: (1) commercial speaker + (2) consumer audience + (3) commercial content = §17500 applies. No First Amendment shield for false commercial speech.

case_law.cite: Williams v. Gerber Products Co., 552 F.3d 934 (9th Cir. 2008)
case_law.court: United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit
case_law.key_rule: Reasonable consumer test: significant portion of the public acting reasonably could be misled. Back-label disclosure does not cure front-label deception. Deception by implication actionable.

case_law.cite: In re Tobacco II Cases, 46 Cal.4th 298 (2009)
case_law.key_rule: Post-Prop 64 reliance requirement: class representative must show personal reliance on specific misrepresentations; absent class members exempt from individual reliance; purchase price = 'lost money'; direct-recipient reliance (point-of-sale misrepresentation) satisfies causation.
